claim: A near atomic structure of the active human apoptosome was determined by cryo-electron microscopy at a global resolution of ~4.1 Å.
source: Here we report a near atomic structure of the active human apoptosome determined by cryo-electron microscopy.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states the structure was determined by cryo-EM, and Figure 1—figure supplement 1C shows the gold standard FSC curve indicating 4.1 Å resolution.

claim: During activation, an acentric disk is formed on the central hub of the apoptosome.
source: During activation an acentric disk is formed on the central hub of the apoptosome.
evidence: This is directly stated in the abstract and supported by structural data shown in Figures 1 and 7.

claim: The acentric disk contains four Apaf-1/pc-9 CARD pairs arranged in a shallow spiral with the fourth pc-9 CARD at lower occupancy.
source: This disk contains four Apaf-1/pc-9 CARD pairs arranged in a shallow spiral with the fourth pc-9 CARD at lower occupancy.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this arrangement, which is supported by structural analysis in Figures 7 and 8.

claim: Apaf-1 CARDs recruit 3 to 5 pc-9 molecules to the apoptosome on average.
source: On average, Apaf-1 CARDs recruit 3 to 5 pc-9 molecules to the apoptosome and one catalytic domain may be parked on the hub, when an odd number of zymogens are bound.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by stoichiometry measurements cited in the introduction (Malladi et al., 2009; Yuan et al., 2011a; Hu et al., 2014).

claim: One catalytic domain may be parked on the hub when an odd number of zymogens are bound.
source: On average, Apaf-1 CARDs recruit 3 to 5 pc-9 molecules to the apoptosome and one catalytic domain may be parked on the hub, when an odd number of zymogens are bound.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by structural data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1.

claim: The stoichiometry suggests one or at most two pc-9 dimers per active apoptosome.
source: This suggests a stoichiometry of one or at most, two pc-9 dimers per active apoptosome.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and is an inference based on the structural data and stoichiometry measurements.

claim: Programmed cell death occurs during tissue development and homeostasis to remove superfluous cells.
source: Programmed cell death occurs during tissue development and homeostasis to remove superfluous cells or alternatively, during disease states to remove damaged or rapidly dividing cells (Song and Stellar, 1999; Salvesen and Dixit, 1997; Green and Evan, 2002; Danial and Korsmeyer, 2004; Thompson, 1995).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with multiple supporting citations.

claim: Programmed cell death allows cellular components to be recycled without activating inflammatory pathways.
source: In general, this process allows cellular components to be recycled without activating inflammatory pathways (Green and Evan, 2002; Inohara and Nuñez, 2003).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Intrinsic cell death signals converge on mitochondria to release pro-apoptotic factors through outer membrane pores formed by Bcl-2 family members.
source: In humans, intrinsic cell death signals converge on mitochondria to release pro-apoptotic factors through outer membrane pores formed by Bcl-2 family members (Brunelle and Letai, 2009; Tait and Green, 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Cytochrome c up-regulates assembly of Apaf-1 to form the apoptosome.
source: These factors include cytochrome c, which up-regulates assembly of the Apoptotic protease activation factor-1 (Apaf-1) to form the apoptosome (Li et al., 1997).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: Apaf-1 is a member of the AAA+ ATPase family and has seven domains.
source: Apaf-1 is a member of the AAA+ ATPase family, has seven domains and exists as an inactive monomer in the cytoplasm of healthy cells (Danot et al., 2009; Leipe et al., 2004).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Apaf-1 exists as an inactive monomer in the cytoplasm of healthy cells.
source: Apaf-1 is a member of the AAA+ ATPase family, has seven domains and exists as an inactive monomer in the cytoplasm of healthy cells (Danot et al., 2009; Leipe et al., 2004).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Cytochrome c binding to β-propellers in Apaf-1 may trigger nucleotide exchange with ATP/dATP replacing bound ADP/dADP.
source: When released, cytochrome c binds to β-propellers in Apaf-1 and may trigger nucleotide exchange with ATP/dATP replacing bound ADP/dADP (Liu et al., 1996; Li et al., 1997; Zou et al., 1997, 1999; Hu et al., 1998, 1999).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Nucleotide exchange leads to the assembly of a heptameric apoptosome.
source: This leads to the assembly of a heptameric apoptosome (Acehan et al., 2002).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: CARD-CARD interactions target inactive pc-9 monomers to the apoptosome.
source: Thus, CARD-CARD interactions target inactive pc-9 monomers to the apoptosome (Yuan et al., 2011a; Hu et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: A CARD disk is formed that sits above the central hub and is attached by linkers to the nucleotide binding domain.
source: During this step, a CARD 'disk' is formed that sits above the central hub, and is attached by linkers to the nucleotide binding domain (NBD) (Yuan et al., 2010, 2011a, 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: The global 3D refinement produced a map with a global resolution of 4.1 Å as determined with a gold standard FSC.
source: These particles were 'polished' and refined with seven-fold symmetry (c7) in RELION to produce a map with a global resolution of 4.1 Å, as determined with a gold standard FSC (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C; Scheres, 2014, 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by the FSC curve in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claim: The central hub is at a nominal resolution of 3–4 Å.
source: As estimated by ResMap (Kucukelbir et al., 2014) the central hub is at a nominal resolution of 3–4 Å and this is supported by the visibility of larger side chains.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by ResMap analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1E.

claim: The extended arm and peripheral sensor domains are in the range of 4.5–10 Å resolution.
source: The extended arm and peripheral sensor domains are in the range of 4.5–10 Å resolution (Figure 1—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by ResMap analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1E.

claim: The apoptosome has dimensions of 270 x 270 x ~75 Å.
source: A sharpened and normalized 3D map from the global 3D refinement was rendered as an iso-surface to show the wheel-like geometry of the apoptosome, which has dimensions of 270 x 270 x ~75 Å.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on the structural data.

claim: Focused 3D classification allowed obtaining an improved density map with a resolution of ~6.1 Å for the sensor domain.
source: However, a focused 3D classification (Materials and methods; Zhou et al., 2015) allowed us to obtain an improved density map with a resolution of ~6.1 Å for this region.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by the FSC curve in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claim: The active apoptosome contains an acentric disk formed by Apaf-1 and pc-9 CARDs.
source: However, the active apoptosome contains an acentric disk formed by Apaf-1 and pc-9 CARDs, with a catalytic domain of pc-9 bound to the central hub in some particles (as discussed later; Yuan et al., 2010, 2011a, 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by structural data in Figures 7 and 8.

claim: The heptameric platform appears to be mostly unchanged during pc-9 activation relative to the ground state, with an rmsd of 1.7 Å for Cα's.
source: The heptameric platform appears to be mostly unchanged during pc-9 activation relative to the ground state, with an rmsd of 1.7 Å for Cα's, when comparing Apaf-1 and cytochrome c in the two complexes (Zhou et al., 2015; this work).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on comparison with the ground state structure.

claim: The central hub of the apoptosome contains seven copies of the NBD, HD1 and WHD in two nested rings.
source: The central hub of the apoptosome 'wheel' contains seven copies of the NBD, HD1 and WHD in two nested rings (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3A.

claim: HD2 forms an arm in each subunit that extends outwards from the hub and ends in a V-shaped sensor domain formed by 7- and 8-blade β-propellers with cytochrome c bound between them.
source: In addition, HD2 forms an arm in each subunit that extends outwards from the hub and ends in a V-shaped sensor domain formed by 7- and 8-blade β-propellers with cytochrome c bound between them (Figure 2 and Figure 2—figure supplements 1, 2).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figures 2 and 4.

claim: The central hub is formed by lateral interactions between adjacent NBDs including a ring of paired α-helices that surrounds the central pore.
source: The central hub is formed by lateral interactions between adjacent NBDs including a ring of paired α-helices that surrounds the central pore (Figure 3B,C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3B,C.

claim: The cylindrical picket-fence is formed by helix α12, the initiator specific motif (ISM), which is connected to helix α13 by a long loop that lines the pore itself.
source: This cylindrical picket-fence is formed by helix α12, the initiator specific motif (ISM; Danot et al., 2009), which is connected to helix α13 by a long loop that lines the pore itself.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3.

claim: The two α-helices in the ISM motif are held together by a hydrophobic interface.
source: The two α-helices in this motif are held together by a hydrophobic interface (Figure 3D), while an extensive network of hydrogen bonds and salt bridges mediate interactions between adjacent α12-loop-α13 motifs (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3D.

claim: An extensive network of hydrogen bonds and salt bridges mediate interactions between adjacent α12-loop-α13 motifs.
source: The two α-helices in this motif are held together by a hydrophobic interface (Figure 3D), while an extensive network of hydrogen bonds and salt bridges mediate interactions between adjacent α12-loop-α13 motifs (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3E.

claim: The nucleotide dATP is bound in a pocket at the interface between the NBD and HD1.
source: The nucleotide dATP is bound in a pocket at the interface between the NBD and HD1.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5.

claim: An outer ring in the hub is formed by interactions between an HD1 and the WHD in adjacent subunits.
source: An outer ring in the hub is formed by interactions between an HD1 and the WHD in adjacent subunits to compliment extensive interactions between HD1-WHD pairs in each subunit (Figure 3F).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3F.

claim: The HD1-WHD loop is involved in dATP binding and interacts with the NBD of an adjacent monomer.
source: The HD1-WHD loop is involved in dATP binding and interacts with the NBD of an adjacent monomer.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3G,H.

claim: The WHD-HD2 interface is similar to that observed in crystal structures of an inactive Apaf-1.
source: Also note that the WHD-HD2 interface is similar to that observed in crystal structures of an inactive Apaf-1 (Riedl et al., 2005; Reubold et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with supporting citations.

claim: Sensor domains in the apoptosome are formed by 15 WD40 repeats that form tandem 7- and 8-blade β-propellers in the C-terminal half of the molecule.
source: Sensor domains in the apoptosome are formed by 15 WD40 repeats that form tandem 7- and 8-blade β-propellers in the C-terminal half of the molecule (Yuan et al., 2011a, 2013; Reubold et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with supporting citations.

claim: Cytochrome c is located between the two β-propellers.
source: Cytochrome c is released from mitochondria to trigger apoptosome assembly from Apaf-1 monomers in the cytoplasm and is located between the two β-propellers (Yuan et al., 2010, 2013; Zhou et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with supporting citations and shown in Figure 4.

claim: All α-helices in cytochrome c are resolved when the map is viewed at a much higher threshold.
source: All α-helices in cytochrome c are resolved when the map is viewed at a much higher threshold (not shown) and the overall fit is similar in ground state and active apoptosomes (this work, Zhou et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on structural analysis.

claim: A rotation of ~90 degrees was required to position cytochrome c, relative to the previous model.
source: Importantly, a rotation of ~90 degrees was required to position cytochrome c, relative to our previous model, due to an ambiguity in the two top docking solutions when fitting with a map at a global resolution of 9.5–10 Å (Yuan et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on comparison with the previous model.

claim: Cytochrome c appears to interact preferentially with the 8-blade β-propeller through an extensive contact region.
source: The cytochrome c molecule appears to interact preferentially with the 8-blade β-propeller through an extensive contact region, which is apparent when the map is viewed at a lower threshold, which provides a better estimate of the all atom volume (boxed region 1, Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Contacts to the 8-blade β-propeller are more extensive and involve numerous van der Waals interactions.
source: However, contacts to the 8-blade β-propeller are more extensive and involve numerous van der Waals interactions, while a gap of ~3–5 Å is present over much of the interface between cytochrome c and the 7-blade β-propeller (Figure 4D, interfaces labeled 1 and 2, respectively).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 4D.

claim: A gap of ~3–5 Å is present over much of the interface between cytochrome c and the 7-blade β-propeller.
source: However, contacts to the 8-blade β-propeller are more extensive and involve numerous van der Waals interactions, while a gap of ~3–5 Å is present over much of the interface between cytochrome c and the 7-blade β-propeller (Figure 4D, interfaces labeled 1 and 2, respectively).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Seven lysines from cytochrome c are found in the major contact regions and include: lysines 25, 27, 39, 55, 72, 73 and 79.
source: In total, 7 lysines from cytochrome c are found in the major contact regions and include: lysines 25, 27, 39, 55, 72, 73 and 79 (also see Yu et al., 2001).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a supporting citation.

claim: Cytochrome c binding has a direct impact on the structure of the β-propellers, relative to their conformation in a crystal structure of unliganded Apaf-1.
source: Cytochrome c binding has a direct impact on the structure of the β-propellers, relative to their conformation in a crystal structure of unliganded Apaf-1 (Reubold et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a supporting citation.

claim: An overlay of 7-blade β-propellers without and with bound cytochrome c shows a symmetric radial displacement with an rmsd of 1.9 Å.
source: An overlay of 7-blade β-propellers without and with bound cytochrome c shows a symmetric radial displacement with an rmsd of 1.9 Å (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 4E.

claim: The dATP binding site in Apaf-1 is located at the NBD-HD1 interface and is formed in part by the Walker A loop and the HD1-WHD loop.
source: The dATP binding site in Apaf-1 is located at the NBD-HD1 interface and is formed in part by the Walker A loop and the HD1-WHD loop (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5A.

claim: The adenine base is bound in a deep hydrophobic pocket lined by NBD residues Pro120, Pro123, Phe126, Val127, Val162, Leu163, Leu286, Lys290, Ileu294 along with Pro321 from HD1.
source: In particular, the adenine base is bound in a deep hydrophobic pocket lined by NBD residues Pro120, Pro123, Phe126, Val127, Val162, Leu163, Leu286, Lys290, Ileu294 along with Pro321 from HD1 (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5C.

claim: The adenine base is in an anti configuration relative to the deoxyribose ring and makes hydrogen bonds to the backbone carbonyl and amide of Val127.
source: The adenine base is in an anti configuration relative to the deoxyribose ring and makes hydrogen bonds to the backbone carbonyl and amide of Val127 to help position the fused rings (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5D.

claim: A conserved arginine (Arg129) is located above the adenine base at the 'top' of the pocket and plays a structural role.
source: A conserved arginine (Arg129) is located above the adenine base at the 'top' of the pocket and plays a structural role.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on structural analysis.

claim: The anti orientation of the adenine base is present in crystal structures of Apaf-1 with bound ADP and in near atomic structures of Dark and CED-4 apoptosomes.
source: We note that the anti orientation of the adenine base is present in crystal structures of Apaf-1 with bound ADP (Riedl et al., 2005; Reubold et al., 2011) and in near atomic structures of Dark and CED-4 apoptosomes (Cheng et al., unpublished; Qi et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with supporting citations.

claim: The HD1-WHD loop forms the bottom of the nucleotide binding pocket.
source: In our model, the HD1-WHD loop forms the bottom of the nucleotide binding pocket.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Tyr359 in the HD1 may act as a sensor for dATP akin to sensor I (Arg265) in the NBD.
source: Thus, Tyr359 in the HD1 may act as a sensor for dATP akin to sensor I (Arg265) in the NBD.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on structural analysis shown in Figure 5B,D.

claim: The side chain of Ser325 in helix α18 is located within ~4 Å of the 2' carbon of the deoxyribose ring.
source: Importantly, the side chain of Ser325 in helix α18 is located within ~4 Å of the 2' carbon of the deoxyribose ring, and is held in position by hydrogen bonds with the 3' OH in the sugar ring and the backbone carbonyl of Leu322 (Figure 5B,D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5B,D.

claim: Ser325 may interact with the 2' OH of the ribose ring when ATP is bound instead of dATP.
source: In addition, Ser325 may interact with the 2' OH of the ribose ring when ATP is bound instead of dATP, as found in the crystal structure of Apaf-1 with ADP (Riedl et al., 2005; Reubold et al., 2011; Figure 5—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with supporting citations and shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2A.

claim: The close apposition of Ser325 to the 2' carbon of the deoxyribose ring may be responsible for the higher affinity exhibited by Apaf-1 for dATP over ATP.
source: The close apposition of Ser325 to the 2' carbon of the deoxyribose ring may be responsible for the higher affinity exhibited by Apaf-1 for dATP over ATP (Jiang and Wang, 2000).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a supporting citation.

claim: Ser325 may act as a modulator that defines the relative affinity for dATP and ATP during assembly of Apaf-1 and Dark apoptosomes.
source: Thus, Ser325 may act as a modulator that defines the relative affinity for dATP and ATP during assembly of Apaf-1 and Dark apoptosomes.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on structural analysis and comparison with Dark.

claim: The Apaf-1 monomer has very limited ATPase activity (~4–5 ATPs/Apaf-1/hr).
source: The Apaf-1 monomer has very limited ATPase activity (~4–5 ATPs/Apaf-1/hr; Reubold et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a supporting citation.

claim: No arginine finger is contributed by an adjacent monomer in the apoptosome to promote catalysis.
source: In support of this data, no arginine finger is contributed by an adjacent monomer in the apoptosome to promote catalysis.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on structural analysis.

claim: No clear density is present in the map of the human apoptosome for a Mg+2 ion.
source: Importantly, no clear density is present in our map of the human apoptosome for a Mg+2 ion and modeling with this ion in a previous structure appears to have distorted the model for dATP (Zhou et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on structural analysis.

claim: Cytochrome c binding and nucleotide exchange produce a large conformational change in Apaf-1.
source: In the current assembly model, cytochrome c binding and nucleotide exchange produce a large conformational change in Apaf-1 (Yuan et al., 2013; Pang et al., 2015; Reubold et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with supporting citations.

claim: Cytochrome c binding is a pre-requisite for nucleotide exchange during assembly.
source: We suggest that cytochrome c binding is a pre-requisite for nucleotide exchange during assembly.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on native gel experiments shown in Figure 6A.

claim: A significant band shift and aggregation of Apaf-1 on native gels was observed when cytochrome c was added.
source: In particular, we observed a significant band shift and aggregation of Apaf-1 on native gels when cytochrome c was added, while similar changes could not be detected when dATP was added in a separate reaction.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 6A.

claim: When dATP and cytochrome c are both added, the aggregation pathway is by-passed and a high molecular weight band is formed that corresponds to the apoptosome.
source: When dATP and cytochrome c are both added, the aggregation pathway is by-passed and a high molecular weight band is formed that corresponds to the apoptosome (Figure 6A, lane 8).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Cytochrome c and a bound nucleotide triphosphate would predispose Apaf-1 to adopt an extended conformation that promotes lateral assembly of subunits to form the ring.
source: Thus, cytochrome c and a bound nucleotide triphosphate would predispose Apaf-1 to adopt an extended conformation that promotes lateral assembly of subunits to form the ring.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on structural analysis and native gel experiments.

claim: Near atomic structures of Apaf-1 monomers and the apoptosome suggest that the molecule has diverged from the canonical architecture of AAA+ ATPases.
source: Near atomic structures of Apaf-1 monomers (Riedl et al., 2005; Reubold et al., 2011) and the apoptosome (Zhou et al., 2015; this work) suggest that the molecule has diverged from the canonical architecture of AAA+ ATPases.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with supporting citations.

claim: This includes the 'loss' of a stable binding site for a Mg+2 ion adjacent to the γ-phosphate of dATP/ATP, which greatly diminishes the intrinsic ATPase activity of the monomer.
source: This includes the 'loss' of a stable binding site for a Mg+2 ion adjacent to the γ-phosphate of dATP/ATP, which greatly diminishes the intrinsic ATPase activity of the monomer.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on structural analysis.

claim: No detectable ATPase activity has been found in apoptosomes.
source: Moreover, no detectable ATPase activity has been found in apoptosomes (Reubold et al., 2009; Kim et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with supporting citations.

claim: pc-9 is able to interact with Apaf-1 to form a 1:1 complex and this step is mediated by CARD-CARD interactions.
source: We also find that pc-9 is able to interact with Apaf-1 to form a 1:1 complex and this step is mediated by CARD-CARD interactions.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 6D.

claim: The concentration of pc-9 and Apaf-1 in HeLa cervical cancer cells is estimated to be ~30 nM and ~340 nM, respectively.
source: Remarkably, the concentration of pc-9 and Apaf-1 in HeLa cervical cancer cells is estimated to be ~30 nM and ~340 nM, respectively (Würstle and Rehm, 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a supporting citation.

claim: Focused 3D classification without additional refinements in RELION was used to resolve the disk at ~5.8Å resolution.
source: To resolve the disk at ~5.8Å resolution we used focused 3D classification without additional refinements in RELION (Materials and methods; Scheres, 2012; Zhou et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with supporting citations.

claim: In the resulting map, the acentric disk contains seven well-ordered CARDs arranged as a clockwise spiral when viewed from above.
source: In the resulting map, the acentric disk contains seven well-ordered CARDs arranged as a clockwise spiral when viewed from above.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on structural analysis shown in Figure 7.

claim: A fourth pc-9 CARD is present at lower occupancy so there are four Apaf-1 CARDs and three or four pc-9 CARDs in the disk at any instant.
source: Moreover, a fourth pc-9 CARD is present at lower occupancy so there are four Apaf-1 CARDs and three or four pc-9 CARDs in the disk at any instant.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on structural analysis shown in Figure 7.

claim: Apaf-1 and pc-9 CARDs are present at odd and even positions around the spiral, respectively.
source: Overall, Apaf-1 and pc-9 CARDs are present at odd and even positions around the spiral, respectively, (Figure 8A,B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 8A,B.

claim: Apaf-1/pc-9 CARD pairs are located in positions 1a-2p, 3a-4p, 5a-6p and 7a-8p, where they define a one-start, quasi-helical spiral.
source: In this notation, Apaf-1/pc-9 CARD pairs are located in positions 1a-2p, 3a-4p, 5a-6p and 7a-8p, where they define a one-start, quasi-helical spiral.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on structural analysis shown in Figure 8.

claim: Four of the seven Apaf-1 CARDs in the apoptosome are used to construct the disk.
source: In total, four of the seven Apaf-1 CARDs in the apoptosome are used to construct the disk.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on structural analysis shown in Figure 7.

claim: CARD-NBD linker densities connect the C-terminal α-helix of each CARD to helix α8 of its respective NBD.
source: In addition, CARD-NBD linker densities connect the C-terminal α-helix of each CARD to helix α8 of its respective NBD, when viewed at an appropriate threshold (in gold, Figure 7B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 7B.

claim: The remaining three Apaf-1 CARDs in the apoptosome are not added to the top of the disk to form a third layer, presumably due to restraints imposed by the length of their CARD-NBD linkers.
source: The remaining three Apaf-1 CARDs in the apoptosome are not added to the top of the disk to form a third layer, presumably due to restraints imposed by the length of their CARD-NBD linkers.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on structural analysis.

claim: The three excluded Apaf-1 CARDs are disordered since they are not visible.
source: We surmise that the three excluded Apaf-1 CARDs are disordered since they are not visible, but they may contribute to the propensity of the particles to aggregate.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on structural analysis.

claim: The CARD spiral is located acentrically relative to the seven-fold symmetry axis of the apoptosome and rests in a tilted position on the NBD ring.
source: The CARD spiral is located acentrically relative to the seven-fold symmetry axis of the apoptosome and rests in a tilted position on the NBD ring (Figure 7).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 7.

claim: Only three well ordered pc-9 CARDs and a single more weakly bound molecule are present in the disk.
source: Surprisingly, only three well ordered pc-9 CARDs and a single more weakly bound molecule are present in the disk.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on structural analysis shown in Figure 7.

claim: No direct contacts are present between pc-9 CARDs and the central hub.
source: In addition, no direct contacts are present between pc-9 CARDs and the central hub, and all pc-9 domains are located on the top surface of the disk-like spiral with their N- and C-termini pointing towards the outside.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on structural analysis.

claim: The overall architecture of the disk is distinct from a recent model, which suggested that the disk would contain three layers of alternating Apaf-1, pc-9 and Apaf-1 CARDs.
source: The overall architecture of the disk is distinct from a recent model, which suggested that the disk would contain three layers of alternating Apaf-1, pc-9 and Apaf-1 CARDs (Hu et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a supporting citation.

claim: Type II interfaces occur between CARDs in color-coded pairs.
source: The disposition of Type I and II interfaces in the disk is shown in Figures 7C and 8B–D with Type II interfaces occurring between CARDs in color-coded pairs (Figure 8A,B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figures 7C and 8B–D.

claim: The interfaces become more distorted in moving clockwise around the disk from position 1a, due to the spiral geometry of the CARDs.
source: In general, the interfaces become more distorted in moving clockwise around the disk from position 1a, due to the spiral geometry of the CARDs.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on structural analysis.

claim: The CARD spiral results in a rather open interface between two adjacent pc-9 CARDs at positions 8p-2p.
source: The CARD spiral results in a rather open interface between two adjacent pc-9 CARDs at positions 8p-2p, and a novel interface is formed between Apaf-1 CARDs at positions 7a-1a (Figure 8E,F).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 8E,F.

claim: A novel interface is formed between Apaf-1 CARDs at positions 7a-1a.
source: The CARD spiral results in a rather open interface between two adjacent pc-9 CARDs at positions 8p-2p, and a novel interface is formed between Apaf-1 CARDs at positions 7a-1a (Figure 8E,F).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 8E,F.

claim: Mutations that disrupt Type I and Type II interfaces are supported by the model of the disk.
source: Hence, mutations that disrupt Type I and Type II interfaces are supported by our model of the disk.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on structural analysis and comparison with mutation studies.

claim: Two additional Apaf-1 CARD mutations (K58E, K62E) were found to greatly diminish pc-9 activation and occur outside of interfaces I and II.
source: Two additional Apaf-1 CARD mutations (K58E, K62E) were found to greatly diminish pc-9 activation and occur outside of interfaces I and II (Hu et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a supporting citation.

claim: These mutations are located on the bottom surface of the disk-like spiral and may interfere with Apaf-1 CARD interactions to the NBD ring.
source: These mutations are located on the bottom surface of the disk-like spiral and may interfere with Apaf-1 CARD interactions to the NBD ring.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on structural analysis.

claim: Density for catalytic domains of a single pc-9 could be identified on the central hub, adjacent to the disk.
source: We showed previously that density for catalytic domains of a single pc-9 could be identified on the central hub, adjacent to the disk (Yuan et al., 2011a, 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with supporting citations.

claim: A similar feature for pc-9 was found on the central hub with the large data set, and the density accommodates a single copy of the p20/p10 domains.
source: A similar feature for pc-9 was found on the central hub with this large data set, and the density accommodates a single copy of the p20/p10 domains.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on structural analysis shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1.

claim: The catalytic domain can be located in two possible positions that are adjacent to a pc-9 CARD at position 2p within the CARD disk.
source: Intriguingly, the catalytic domain can be located in two possible positions that are adjacent to a pc-9 CARD at position 2p within the CARD disk.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on structural analysis shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1B,C.

claim: Only ~50% of the particles contained the density in the aligned location.
source: We also surmise that pc-9 catalytic domains may be bound in a dynamic manner, since only ~50% of the particles contained the density in the aligned location.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on structural analysis.

claim: The structure of an active apoptosome provides additional insights into the mechanism of pc-9 activation.
source: Our structure of an active apoptosome provides additional insights into the mechanism of pc-9 activation.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section.

claim: Stoichiometry measurements indicate that a range of 2 to 5 pc-9 molecules may be bound to the apoptosome.
source: One constraint is provided by stoichiometry measurements, which indicate that a range of 2 to 5 pc-9 molecules may be bound to the apoptosome (Malladi et al., 2009; Yuan et al., 2011a; Hu et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with supporting citations.

claim: The structure suggests that 3 or 4 pc-9 molecules may be tethered to the disk through CARD-CARD interactions.
source: In line with this data, our structure suggests that 3 or 4 pc-9 molecules may be tethered to the disk through CARD-CARD interactions, with the caveat that a pc-9 molecule might also interact with Apaf-1 CARDs that are excluded from the disk.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section based on structural analysis.

claim: Parked catalytic domains could be attached to pc-9 CARDs located at all possible positions in the disk, due to the length of the CARD-p20 linker.
source: One implication of this finding is that parked catalytic domains could be attached to pc-9 CARDs located at all possible positions in the disk, due to the length of the CARD-p20 linker.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section based on structural analysis.

claim: Parked pc-9 catalytic domains may be held in reserve when an odd number of zymogens are bound to the apoptosome.
source: Hence, the most favored parking sites are generally available to all four pc-9 molecules that may be tethered to the disk. We hypothesize that parked pc-9 catalytic domains may be held in reserve when an odd number of zymogens are bound to the apoptosome.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a hypothesis based on structural analysis.

claim: The remaining pc-9 catalytic domains are flexibly-tethered to the disk through CARD-p20 linkers.
source: Thus, we surmise that the remaining pc-9 catalytic domains are flexibly-tethered to the disk through CARD-p20 linkers.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section based on structural analysis.

claim: The active apoptosome is a dynamic proteolytic machine with flexibly-tethered pc-9 catalytic domains, whose nature may depend upon the number of pc-9 molecules that are bound at any instant.
source: We propose that the active apoptosome is a dynamic proteolytic machine with flexibly-tethered pc-9 catalytic domains, whose nature may depend upon the number of pc-9 molecules that are bound at any instant.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a proposal based on structural analysis.

claim: A flexibly-tethered pc-9 dimer may form when three pc-9 molecules are anchored to form a 7 CARD disk.
source: For example, a flexibly-tethered pc-9 dimer may form when three pc-9 molecules are anchored to form a 7 CARD disk, with the pc-9 catalytic domains that are odd man out occupying a parking spot on the central hub (Figure 9, left).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and shown in Figure 9.

claim: If four pc-9 molecules are bound to the apoptosome they may form an 8-CARD disk with two flexibly-tethered pc-9 dimers.
source: However, if four pc-9 molecules are bound to the apoptosome they may form an 8-CARD disk with two flexibly-tethered pc-9 dimers, while leaving open parking spots on the central hub (Figure 9, right).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and shown in Figure 9.

claim: Active apoptosomes with three bound pc-9 molecules were formed with a higher likelihood under the in vitro conditions.
source: Since the pc-9 CARD at position 8p in the disk is present at lower occupancy, it is clear that active apoptosomes with three bound pc-9 molecules were formed with a higher likelihood under our in vitro conditions.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section based on structural analysis.

claim: Apoptosomes with a 7 CARD disk and three pc-9 molecules may be favored in vivo.
source: At the same time, the high protein concentration in our experiments may have aided the formation of an 8 CARD disk in particles with four pc-9 molecules, whereas apoptosomes with a 7 CARD disk and three pc-9 molecules may be favored in vivo.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as speculation based on structural analysis.

claim: Activation of pc-9 on the apoptosome has been proposed to follow the dictates of a molecular timer.
source: Activation of pc-9 on the apoptosome has been proposed to follow the dictates of a molecular timer.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section.

claim: Auto-processing of pc-9 on the apoptosome triggers activation and subsequent release via exchange with unprocessed pc-9 in solution.
source: In this model, auto-processing of pc-9 on the apoptosome triggers activation and subsequent release via exchange with unprocessed pc-9 in solution (Malladi et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with a supporting citation.

claim: The rapid nature of the auto-proteolysis reaction suggests that two-chain pc-9 molecules may account for most of the activity towards procaspase-3.
source: The rapid nature of the auto-proteolysis reaction suggests that two-chain pc-9 molecules, as used in our structure (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A), may account for most of the activity towards procaspase-3 (Malladi et al., 2009; Hu et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with supporting citations.

claim: The structure of the active apoptosome suggests that flexibly-bound pc-9 catalytic domains are probably not able to affect the stability of the CARD-CARD disk.
source: Our structure of the active apoptosome suggests that flexibly-bound pc-9 catalytic domains are probably not able to affect the stability of the CARD-CARD disk.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section based on structural analysis.

claim: pc-9 molecules with shortened CARD-p20 linkers are not activated on the apoptosome as readily as wild type pc-9.
source: Finally, pc-9 molecules with shortened CARD-p20 linkers are not activated on the apoptosome as readily as wild type pc-9 (Yuan et al., 2011a).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with a supporting citation.

claim: The requirement for a somewhat longer spacer may reflect the disposition of the four pc-9 CARD binding sites on the disk.
source: This suggests that the CARD-p20 linker may facilitate pc-9 activation by providing a suitable spacer between CARDs in the disk and the catalytic domains. Indeed, the requirement for a somewhat longer spacer may reflect the disposition of the four pc-9 CARD binding sites on the disk.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as speculation based on structural analysis.

claim: A single clip in the linker releases the catalytic (p20/p10) domains from the apoptosome and results in a complete loss of proteolytic activity.
source: In either case, a single clip in the linker releases the catalytic (p20/p10) domains from the apoptosome and results in a complete loss of proteolytic activity (Yuan et al., 2010, 2011a).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with supporting citations.

claim: Putative pc-9 dimers are only stable when present at a high local concentration on the apoptosome.
source: This argues that putative pc-9 dimers are only stable when present at a high local concentration on the apoptosome.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as an inference based on experimental data.

claim: The structure of an active apoptosome suggests that most complexes will contain one (or possibly two) pc-9 dimers, which may be responsible for proteolytic activity and initiation of a cell death cascade.
source: In summary, our structure of an active apoptosome suggests that most complexes will contain one (or possibly two) pc-9 dimers, which may be responsible for proteolytic activity and initiation of a cell death cascade.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a summary based on structural analysis.
